reason: The instruction scores propositional content about how the rule would actually be executed -- whether the comment names transition steps, testing scenarios, responsible offices, or timelines the agency would have to resolve -- which is the core informational function notice-and-comment exists to collect and is close to the legal notion of a significant comment an agency must address. It references nothing about the submitter, credentials, letterhead, length, formatting, or form-letter status, so a judge cannot score it without comprehending what is being proposed; the proposer's own exemplars (form routing across military services, HVAC failure tests and acceptable proof, application-tracking timelines) are substantive on their face. The identity load is real but derivative: operational detail correlates with sophisticated filers because those filers more often possess the content, and routing every merit criterion that correlates with filer sophistication to Track B would empty the bank of exactly the criteria that define comment quality. The residual risk is that raw specificity can be scored without checking the detail's relevance or correctness -- a precision limit of this rubric worth flagging, not evidence that it measures who wrote the comment.
